questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a part of the All India Services?
questions.solution: The Indian Engineering Service is NOT an All India Service. In India, there are only three All India Services: the Indian Administrative Service (IAS), Indian Police Service (IPS), and Indian Forest Service (IFoS). Note: Members of these services are recruited by the Centre but serve under both State and Central governments.

questions.question: Which is NOT correct about the High Court?
questions.option_1: It can deal with cases within the jurisdiction of the state.
questions.option_2: It gives advisory opinion to the President of India.
questions.option_3: It can issue various writs for the protection of the Fundamental Rights.
questions.option_4: It can hear appeals from the lower courts.
questions.solution: The statement that the High Court 'gives advisory opinion to the President of India' is NOT correct. Only the Supreme Court has advisory jurisdiction under Article 143. High Courts deal with state-level cases, issue writs (Article 226), and hear appeals from subordinate courts.

questions.question: Who among the following appoints the Election Commissioners of India?
questions.solution: The President of India appoints the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners. They usually have a tenure of six years or up to the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier. Note: The President also has the power to determine the conditions of service and tenure of office of the commissioners.

questions.question: The Constitution provides for reservation of seats in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies for the:
questions.solution: The Constitution provides for the reservation of seats in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies for Scheduled Tribes (ST) and Scheduled Castes (SC). Context: Article 330 provides for reservations in the Lok Sabha, while Article 332 provides for reservations in the State Legislative Assemblies.

questions.question: Which of the following Fundamental Duty provisions is similar to Article 21A?
questions.solution: Article 51A (k) is the Fundamental Duty that mirrors Article 21A. Article 21A makes education a fundamental right for children aged 6–14, and Article 51A (k) makes it a duty for parents or guardians to provide education opportunities to their children in the same age group.

questions.question: In which year was the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights established?
questions.solution: The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) was established in 2007 under the Commission for Protection of Child Rights (CPCR) Act, 2005. Its primary mandate is to ensure that all Laws, Policies, Programmes, and Administrative Mechanisms are in consonance with the Child Rights perspectives.

questions.question: Which of the following Fundamental Rights CANNOT be suspended even when ‘Emergency’ is declared in the country?
questions.solution: Articles 20 and 21 are the only Fundamental Rights that CANNOT be suspended even during a National Emergency. Article 20 deals with protection in respect of conviction for offences, and Article 21 guarantees the right to life and personal liberty. History: This safeguard was added by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978.

questions.question: Which of the following was originally a Fundamental Right, but in 1978 was made a legal right as per Article 300A?
questions.solution: The Right to Property was originally a Fundamental Right under Article 19(1)(f) and Article 31. However, the 44th Amendment Act, 1978 removed it from the list of Fundamental Rights and made it a legal right under Article 300A.

questions.question: A Supreme Court or High Court judge can be removed by the Parliament by:
questions.option_4: both simple and two third majority
questions.solution: A judge of the Supreme Court or a High Court can be removed from office only by an order of the President, passed after an address by each House of Parliament supported by a special majority. This means a majority of the total membership of that House and a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting.

questions.question: How much time was taken to frame the Constitution of India?
questions.solution: The Constituent Assembly took 2 years, 11 months, and 17 days (often rounded to 18 days) to complete the historic task of drafting the Constitution for Independent India. During this period, they held 11 sessions covering a total of 165 days.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India abolishes the concept of ‘untouchability’ and prohibits its practice in any shape or form?
questions.solution: Article 17 of the Constitution abolishes 'untouchability' and forbids its practice in any form. The enforcement of any disability arising out of 'untouchability' is considered an offence punishable in accordance with the law. It is an absolute right that protects against social discrimination.

questions.question: Which of the following Fundamental Duty provisions has laid down that all Indians need to show respect to the Indian National Flag and the Indian National Anthem?
questions.solution: Article 51A (a) requires every citizen to abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag, and the National Anthem. This is the first of the Fundamental Duties listed in Part IV-A.

questions.question: How many times the term judicial review is mentioned in the Constitution?
questions.solution: The term 'Judicial Review' is nowhere mentioned in the Constitution. However, the power of judicial review is derived from several articles, such as Article 13, 32, 131-136, and 226, which empower the courts to strike down unconstitutional laws or executive orders.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a type of Parliamentary question?
questions.solution: 'Long notice question' is NOT a type of Parliamentary question. The valid types are: (1) Starred questions (require oral answers), (2) Unstarred questions (require written answers), and (3) Short notice questions (asked with a notice of less than 10 days).

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT correct about Fundamental Duties?
questions.option_1: Their inclusion in the Constitution was inspired by the American Constitution.
questions.option_3: They were included by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976.
questions.option_4: They are mentioned under Article 51A of the Constitution.
questions.solution: The statement that Fundamental Duties were 'inspired by the American Constitution' is NOT correct. They were actually inspired by the Constitution of the USSR (Soviet Union). Truths: They are non-justiciable, were added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976, and are found in Article 51A.

questions.question: Under whose leadership was the 42nd Amendment Act passed?
questions.solution: The 42nd Amendment Act (1976) was passed under the leadership of Indira Gandhi during the period of Internal Emergency. It brought such wide-ranging changes that it is often called a 'Mini-Constitution'.

questions.question: Under which Article of the Constitution of India is the National Commission for Scheduled Castes established?
questions.solution: Article 338 of the Indian Constitution provides for the establishment of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC). Related: Article 338A deals with the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes, and Article 338B with the National Commission for Backward Classes.

questions.question: As of April 2022, which of the following features of citizenship given in the Constitution of India is NOT true?
questions.option_1: People can benefit from the development of advantages merely by becoming citizens.
questions.option_2: The UK Constitution inspired this notion of citizenship.
questions.option_3: The ability to vote and be elected to positions such as President and Member of Parliament is accessible to Indians around the world.
questions.option_4: The Constitution of India provides for single citizenship.
questions.solution: The statement that 'Indians around the world' can vote or be elected as President/MP is NOT true. While NRIs can vote (if registered), only citizens residing in India who meet specific age and eligibility criteria can be elected to high offices like the President or Member of Parliament.

questions.question: Which of the following has similarity to Article 29(1) of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights which states “everyone has duties to the community in which alone the free and full development of his personality is possible”?
questions.solution: Fundamental Duties are similar to Article 29(1) of the UDHR, as both emphasize that an individual has duties to the community. The Indian Constitution acknowledges through Article 51A that the full development of a citizen is tied to their contribution and responsibility toward society.

questions.question: Which of the followingis NOT true about Right to Religion in India?
questions.option_1: A person may choose any religion or may choose not to follow any religion.
questions.option_2: Freedom to profess, follow and propagate any religion.
questions.option_3: Everyone is free to choose a religion and practice that religion.
questions.solution: The statement that there is 'Freedom for forcible conversions' is NOT true. Article 25 guarantees the right to propagate one's religion, but the Supreme Court has clarified that this does not include the right to forcibly convert another person, as it violates their own freedom of conscience.

questions.question: When was the voting age reduced to 18 in India?
questions.solution: The 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988 (which came into force in 1989) reduced the voting age from 21 to 18 years for the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assembly elections. Purpose: To encourage the participation of India's youth in the democratic process.
